title: A New Family of 3d–4f Bis-Calix[4]arene-Supported Clusters

material_class.structural_family: bis-calix[4]arene-supported 3d–4f cluster (two butterfly fragments linked by a central TbIII)

synthesis.procedure: BisTBC[4] (350 mg, 0.27 mmol, 1 equiv), Cu(NO3)2·3H2O (65 mg, 0.27 mmol, 1 equiv) and Tb(NO3)3·6H2O (245 mg, 0.54 mmol, 2 equiv) were suspended in a 1:1 DMF/MeOH mixture (20 mL) and stirred for 10 minutes. Et3N (0.35 mL) was added and the resulting brown solution was stirred for an additional 2 h and filtered. The mother liquor was allowed to slowly evaporate, affording crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction studies.
synthesis.time: stirred 10 min, then additional 2 h after base addition; slow evaporation of mother liquor
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction followed by filtration and slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; mother liquor allowed to slowly evaporate to give orange needles suitable for X-ray diffraction

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility of polycrystalline 1 at 0.1 T (5–300 K) shows room-temperature χMT = 60.8 cm3 K mol−1, consistent with a [CuII4TbIII5] Curie constant. χMT remains relatively constant until ~175 K then decreases to 46.9 cm3 K mol−1 at 5 K, attributed to competing weak ferro- and antiferromagnetic exchange plus depopulation of TbIII ligand-field sublevels. Magnetization at 2 K does not saturate at 7 T (M = 26.4 μB). No frequency-dependent out-of-phase ac susceptibility; SMM behavior is ruled out.

measurements.conditions: T = 2 K; B = 7 T; does not saturate

material_class.structural_family: bis-calix[4]arene-supported 3d–4f cluster (two Fe2Gd2 butterflies linked by a central FeIII)

synthesis.procedure: BisTBC[4] (350 mg, 0.27 mmol, 1 equiv), Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (109 mg, 0.27 mmol, 1 equiv) and Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (488 mg, 1.08 mmol, 4 equiv) were suspended in a 1:1 DMF/MeOH mixture (20 mL) and stirred for 10 minutes. Et3N (0.35 mL) was added and the resulting orange/brown solution was stirred for an additional 2 h and filtered. The mother liquor was allowed to slowly evaporate, affording crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction studies.
synthesis.time: stirred 10 min, then additional 2 h after base addition; slow evaporation of mother liquor
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction followed by filtration and slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; mother liquor allowed to slowly evaporate to give orange crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT = 53.9 cm3 K mol−1 is consistent with a [FeIII5GdIII4] Curie constant. Upon cooling, χMT remains constant until ~50 K then increases to a maximum of 57 cm3 K mol−1, consistent with competing weak ferro- and antiferromagnetic interactions and little evidence for strong Fe···Fe exchange despite Fe–O–Fe angles of ~130°. Magnetization at 2 K approaches 48.0 μB at 7 T, near the expected maximum S = 53/2 state. No frequency-dependent χM″; SMM behavior is ruled out. Analysis is complicated by disorder of the central Fe3 over two positions.

synthesis.procedure: BisTBC[4] (350 mg, 0.27 mmol, 1 equiv), MnCl2·4H2O (107 mg, 0.54 mmol, 2 equiv) and GdCl3·6H2O (71 mg, 0.27 mmol, 1 equiv) were suspended in a 1:1 DMF/MeOH mixture (20 mL) and stirred for 10 minutes. Et3N (0.35 mL) was added and the resulting purple solution was stirred for an additional 2 h and filtered. The mother liquor was allowed to slowly evaporate, affording crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction studies.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT = 44.0 cm3 K mol−1 is consistent with a [MnIII4GdIII4] Curie constant. χMT remains constant until ~50 K then increases to a maximum of 53 cm3 K mol−1, consistent with competing weak ferro- and antiferromagnetic TM···Ln and Ln···Ln interactions and no direct TM···TM pathways. Magnetization at 2 K approaches 41.6 μB at 7 T, near the expected maximum S = 22 state. No frequency-dependent χM″; SMM behavior is ruled out.
